tasks.short: Supervise students in school spaces and on field trips

steps.what: Read the actual duty assignment, location and relevant supervision instructions
Check the actual space, student group and immediate safety conditions
Supervise students continuously, maintaining visibility and checking safe participation
Respond to immediate needs and guide safe transitions between activities or responsible adults

tasks.design: Configure a direct link from the existing duty assignment to its current supervision instructions in {DOCS}. This removes repeat navigation only; actual student checks, continuous supervision and immediate interventions retain their full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Duty assignments and the applicable instructions may be filed separately even though the supervision itself is entirely situational.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document links can connect the assignment to the correct approved instructions without a model or student monitoring system.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining attention across a moving group and reacting to a child's immediate needs.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices risk, offers reassurance and intervenes physically when needed.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in looking for duty instructions; supervision responsibility and staffing requirements stay unchanged.

reach.task: Understand the supervision arrangements for an unfamiliar school space
reach.learn: Local safeguarding procedures and safe handovers

evidence.claim: A direct link between an existing duty assignment and its instructions can remove navigation without reducing active student supervision. This is model knowledge, not a measured school result.

assumptions: The focal role is the teaching assistant during an ordinary supervision duty. Shares are provisional E1 estimates of that episode, not measured minutes or a staffing reduction. Students' activity and other adults' labour are not part of the focal time denominator.

The duty coordinator already supplies assignment identifier, date, time, location, responsible adult and current instruction reference. The assistant reads and verifies these in s1. The configuration uses only this existing reference; missing or stale references lead to manual lookup within the retained three hours, with no invented clean roster or free data capture.

Of four instruction-access hours per 100 baseline hours, one is repeat navigation removed by the direct link; three remain for reading, checking relevance and fallback. All 96 hours involving actual students and surroundings remain. Test the native link before custom development.

Routine visual checks and headcounts are live supervision, not an invented written attendance register. The existing attendance task is separately enumerated as 22479. This ordinary duty does not establish a routine supervision report, photo record, outward message or automated safety decision. Actual reportable incidents require their real reporting workflow and cannot be treated as free labour here.
unknowns: Are current duty instructions already linked directly?
How often do assignments require a separate instruction lookup?
Which actual incident reports are required during these duties?
research_questions: Does a direct assignment link remove navigation while preserving the correct current instructions?

already_counted.description: Read and verify the duty instructions, including stale-link fallback

incremental.description: Check duty-to-instruction links when instructions move or change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: one navigation hour removed less 0.2 link upkeep leaves 0.8 per 100 focal hours. Conservative case: the assistant already carries the correct duty card, or a field trip uses a separate briefing with no repeated document navigation; keep the existing access route and do not introduce this configuration or its upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Tutor children individually or in small groups to reinforce teachers' learning concepts

steps.what: Open and read the teacher's actual assignment and intended learning concept
Ask children to explain their attempts and identify the immediate misunderstanding
Tutor children through explanations and examples consistent with the teacher's concept
Support children's practice and adapt prompts as their understanding develops
Give spoken feedback and check that children can explain the reinforced concept

tasks.design: Configure a direct assignment link in the existing {LMS} so the assistant reaches the teacher's actual exercise and objective together. Keep explanation, observation, adaptive prompts and spoken feedback human; this introduces no automated assessment or pupil-facing model.
tasks.previous_blocker: An assistant may navigate separately to the exercise and teacher guidance before supporting a pupil.
tasks.enabler_now: Native assignment references can connect existing exercise and objective fields.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding why a child is struggling and choosing a useful explanation without undermining confidence.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant responds to confusion, hesitation and questions in the moment.
tasks.altitude: The same tutoring with slightly less assignment navigation. The teacher retains curriculum and assessment decisions.

reach.task: Support a child through a teacher-selected worked example
reach.learn: Subject explanation, scaffolding and checking understanding

evidence.claim: Native assignment links can reduce navigation to existing guidance; they do not establish that live tutoring takes less time. This estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal episode is actual assignment tutoring. The teacher already provides assignment identifier, exercise version, intended concept and guidance reference through normal teaching preparation. These are read in s1; no machine guesses the objective or profiles pupil ability.

One of ten preparation hours is repeated navigation between exercise and guidance, removed through a native link; nine retain reading, interpretation and manual fallback for missing references. All ninety live tutoring hours remain. The pupil's attempts are directly seen and discussed, not a free transcript or structured assessment feed.

The sibling answer 25-9042.00__2 explicitly models observed progress capture and pupil-record entry under task 22468. No new tutoring log is added here and no saving from that record entry is claimed here. A team roll-up must resolve overlap in observation before combining those tasks.

The episode uses existing exercises and spoken feedback, rather than newly written handouts or written feedback. If actual tutoring includes a separate written feedback artefact, its production and release must be measured rather than hidden in live tutoring. Shares and the one-hour navigation estimate are provisional E1 assumptions.
unknowns: Are exercise and objective already shown together?
How often do assistants need separate written tutoring feedback?
How are progress observations divided between tutoring and the explicit progress-record task?
research_questions: Can the existing assignment view remove navigation without changing the teacher's chosen objective or increasing preparation?

already_counted.description: Assignment reading, objective interpretation and missing-reference fallback

incremental.description: Check assignment-to-guidance links after course changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: ten preparation hours at 90% retain nine, so one hour removed less 0.2 upkeep gives 0.8. Conservative case: the teacher hands over a paper exercise with its guidance already attached, or the native assignment view already has both; retain the current route with no new configuration or upkeep. All child-facing time remains in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enforce school policies and rules governing students

steps.what: Read the applicable current school rule and the assistant's delegated response limits
Observe what happened and hear the student's explanation
Choose a proportionate response within the teacher's delegated rules
Enforce the rule through explanation, redirection and immediate practical support
Enter the actual incident facts and response in the existing pupil record
Save the ordinary factual incident entry in its existing pupil-record location

tasks.design: Configure direct access to current rule sections in {DOCS} and reuse existing pupil and class headers in the actual incident form in {OTHER}, the pupil-record system. Keep the incident account, fairness judgement, response and factual writing human; the ordinary internal save remains fully retained and ungated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule navigation and repeated incident headers surround a response that requires context and delegated human authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Native rule links and record-form defaults can remove repeated access and identity fields without inferring misconduct.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing a child's account fairly, distinguishing observation from inference and responding proportionately.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant preserves dignity and adjusts a response to the immediate situation.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less navigation and repeated typing; discipline and escalation authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Use an assistant's factual incident account when planning follow-up
reach.learn: Neutral observation, safeguarding escalation and separating facts from interpretations

evidence.claim: Existing pupil-record form defaults can reuse identity fields while the author retains factual incident writing and the ordinary save. This is model knowledge, not evidence of local time saved.

assumptions: This represents a documented, delegated rule-enforcement episode for which the school already requires a factual entry read by the teacher for follow-up. It is not a new behaviour log for every verbal reminder. Measure the mix of documented incidents and informal corrections before applying this case estimate to the whole task.

The school administrator supplies the current rule version and delegated limits. The existing pupil-record owner supplies pupil identifier and class through the current authorised record; the assistant verifies identity when opening that record. Incident time, observations, the child's account, response and outcome are produced by the assistant's actual work in s2-s4 and typed in s5, not supplied as a free structured feed.

Rule links remove 0.8 of eight access hours. Form defaults remove 0.99 of nine entry hours for repeated pupil and class headers only; 8.01 hours retain substantive writing, identity checks, missing-default fallback and corrections. The one-hour save is the schema's small positive allocation, fully retained with no self-approval gate.

Test existing native links and defaults before code. No model evaluates student behaviour, recommends sanctions or writes an incident narrative. No formal sanction posting, parent message or external disclosure occurs in this delegated episode; where the real response requires such actions their final payload checks and releases need separate priced steps.

Shares are provisional E1 scenario estimates. Access and national participation requirements for existing child records must be confirmed during rollout; this configuration creates no staff or pupil monitoring service.
unknowns: Which incidents actually require a teacher-read record today?
Are pupil and class already defaulted in the incident form?
Which responses require teacher escalation or parent communication?
research_questions: Do native defaults remove repeated headers without selecting the wrong pupil?
What is the observed time mix of documented incidents and informal rule reminders?

already_counted.description: Actual rule reading and factual record writing, identity verification, correction and missing-default fallback

incremental.description: Check current rule links and pupil-record defaults after policy or form changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: 0.8 rule-navigation plus 0.99 header hours removed less 0.3 upkeep leaves 1.49; high rounds down to 1.4. Conservative case: the incident form already fills identity fields, so all nine entry hours remain, but the separate rule lookup still loses 0.8 hour; less 0.3 upkeep leaves 0.5. Neither case reduces observing, hearing the child, deciding or intervening.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach social skills to students through modelling, practice and feedback

steps.what: Read the teacher's ready-to-use social-skills activity and intended behaviour
Observe the immediate social situation and choose an appropriate teaching moment
Teach social skills by modelling turn-taking, listening or respectful requests
Guide students through actual peer practice and supported role-play
Give immediate spoken feedback and reinforce the skill in the real interaction

tasks.design: Keep the teacher's existing activity directly available in {DOCS} and retain the assistant's actual reading and delivery. A native template cannot shorten the children's social practice or the assistant's observation and feedback in this episode; no new software is justified.
tasks.previous_blocker: Social learning depends on actual peer responses and patient practice rather than copying an artefact.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing ready-to-use activities already support preparation; the digest does not establish a time saving on this live interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Helping a child practise a skill safely while respecting individual differences and the other children.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant demonstrates respectful behaviour and adjusts support in response to what children actually do.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the assistant's week or decision rights from this design.

reach.learn: Developmentally appropriate modelling, inclusive facilitation and safeguarding boundaries

evidence.claim: A document template does not itself replace live modelling, supported peer practice or immediate social feedback. This is model knowledge, not a measured zero-saving study.

assumptions: The focal role delivers a teacher-selected, ready-to-use activity. The teacher already supplies the activity version, intended behaviour and facilitation guidance. s1 explicitly separates reading this actual document from the child-facing work; it is already directly available, so there is no repeated navigation or document creation to remove.

Actual interactions are observed directly in s2-s5. No emotion recognition, behavioural inference model, recording, transcript or automatic social-skills assessment is introduced. No structured student-data feed is assumed.

This delivery episode uses spoken feedback and does not establish a routine written social-skills report. The sibling 22468 explicitly covers observed progress capture and pupil-record entry; new lesson materials are explicitly covered in 22474. Those sibling steps were read, and no saving from their writes is claimed in this delivery task. A roll-up must resolve any overlapping observation effort.

The native-view and template check finds the actual card already available and no manual first write, repeated entry or real send in this episode. Keep all preparation and live time. Incremental upkeep is zero because no configuration, model, integration or new record is introduced; existing material maintenance is unchanged teacher work, not transferred to the assistant.

The five shares are E1 estimates for this activity, not a claim that every school follows this timing. A school that requires a distinct written feedback artefact must count its actual writing separately before reusing this estimate.
unknowns: Are these activities already provided ready to use?
Does local practice require a distinct written report beyond the existing pupil-progress task?
research_questions: Does observation confirm that the actual episode contains only the existing card, live practice and spoken feedback?

incremental.description: No new tool or record; no additional ongoing upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 100 focal hours remain and no incremental work is introduced. The activity card is already directly available; modelling, actual peer practice and immediate feedback all remain. No materials-generation or separate pupil-record saving is assigned to this live delivery episode.

role.altitude: Small reductions in genuine instruction lookup and incident headers leave the assistant's student-facing work and the teacher's decision authority intact.
reach: Support teacher-selected tutoring and social-skills activities
Provide factual incident information within delegated safeguarding procedures
role.ambitious_version: An assistant with easier access to current instructions and unchanged responsibility for attentive, fair and supportive work with children.
